evals.prompt: Capture six CPU physics steps to a new OVD file and show that the file can be inspected.
evals.expected_output: Run installed ovd-record with a new path, check success and verifiedSamples, then ovd-inspect summary on the finalized file.
expectations: Uses ovd-record with an unused output path
Checks command success before inspection
Uses checked, profile or debug SDK rather than Release

evals.prompt: My PhysX scene has already run twenty steps. Record the next two, preserving the final actor state.
evals.expected_output: Explain initial PxOmniPvd attachment, idle late start full snapshot, two completed steps, stopSampling and checked closeStream before teardown.
expectations: Requires PxOmniPvd to have been passed to PxCreatePhysics
Binds a new file stream before startSampling at an idle scene boundary
Checks stopSampling and closeStream before actor or scene teardown
Distinguishes local recorded frames from application step numbers

evals.prompt: Run the headless GPU OVD recording example. Is a no-GPU result enough to say capture works?
evals.expected_output: Run ovd-record with --gpu where supported, report exit77 as unavailable, and keep independent real CPU verification.
expectations: Uses --gpu only with a GPU-capable SDK build
Reports exit77 as a skip, not GPU success
Does not substitute a GPU skip for CPU evidence

evals.prompt: Find the first linear velocity divergence in two existing finalized OVD files.
evals.expected_output: Route to ovd-compare for explicit object matching and frame alignment.
expectations: Selects ovd-compare
Does not recapture or overwrite supplied recordings

evals.prompt: In my existing OmniPVD-enabled SDK app, capture only a robot, one particle buffer and a deformable, without contacts or forces. Can I select one articulation link or request transforms alone? What if I later enable collisions on DirectGPU?
evals.expected_output: Uses a copied PxOmniPvdFilterDesc with selected owning objects and recordSecondaryData=false at a synchronized start; explains whole-articulation, particle-buffer and contact dependency behavior and data limits.
expectations: Passes PxOmniPvdFilterDesc to startSampling after binding the stream, optionally validateFilterDesc under the same external synchronization
Explains scene/object union, all-object empty lists and future members of selected scenes; selects whole articulations, individual particle buffers and deformable actors rather than links/resources
Explains mandatory primary geometry, state and materials, with no transform-only mask; bool recordSecondaryData=true adds all supported secondary data
Includes either-selected-endpoint contacts and required counterpart state without recursively selecting other contacts; selection does not change DirectGPU mode
Distinguishes base particle primary data from secondary diffuse data and states that unrecorded producer payloads cannot be enabled by a filter
Stops and restarts for a local policy change and explicitly closes the owned FILE stream after stop before inspecting

evals.prompt: Connect the SDK producer to a TCP viewer without copying a full GPU scene first. Let the viewer discover/select objects, then replace selection live. How do I service requests, and will an older TCP stream still open?
evals.expected_output: Starts an identity-only startCaptureDiscovery session on the bound TCP stream, pumps processCaptureRequests at an all-scene safe point and waits for applied forward acknowledgments, preserving older one-way producers.
expectations: Starts the listening receiver before the outbound producer connection and uses startCaptureDiscovery(scope) instead of an initial unrestricted startSampling
Explains catalog identities without payload/GPU readback, fixed maximum scope, isSampling=false until selection and stopSampling ending discovery as well as sampling
Uses OmniPvdSocketReadStream.requestCapture with run/connection-local handles and increasing nonzero IDs; requestCaptureCatalog can refresh a supported active discovery catalog

Externally synchronizes processCaptureRequests with every scene, fetchResults including particle fetch, object creation/release and membership changes; a successful poll/send alone does not mean applied
Checks matching captureRequestId, status 1 applied versus 2 invalid/3 busy/4 denied, and captureEpoch; accepted policy writes a fresh snapshot on the same connection
Uses negotiated reverse-control capability rather than just integration-version metadata; unsupported old producers receive no control bytes and remain readable
Does not treat concurrent close of a blocking reader as supported cancellation and does not claim ovd-inspect is a live TCP receiver

evals.prompt: Our plugin writes custom OVD data. Will SDK selection automatically filter those writes? How should we handle a receiver reset and keep the filter or replacement arrays alive?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes raw writer responsibility from built-in filtering, explains event/reset callback locking and temporary descriptors, and the application filter's replacement-array lifetime.
expectations: States raw OmniPvdWriter writes are not filtered automatically; plugin honors onStartSampling's active policy and applicable object selection
Copies any retained callback descriptor/list data rather than retaining temporary pointers
Uses onCaptureReset to retire custom records before replay and ScopedExclusiveWriter for reset callback writes because the writer lock is not held
Keeps PxOmniPvdCaptureFilter replacement arrays valid until processCaptureRequests returns and preserves external synchronization
Does not present isObjectRecorded=false as proof that no counterpart state was emitted
